chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, all of them from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about something from the obligatory inheritance shares, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I bring out for you the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)?' So I said, 'The Book of Ali (peace be upon him) has not been studied.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! The Book of Ali (peace be upon him) has not been studied?' So he (peace be upon him) brought it out, and it was a splendid book, and therein was: a man who died and left his paternal uncle and his maternal uncle. He (peace be upon him) said: 'For the paternal uncle is two-thirds and for the maternal uncle is the one-third'.

key_terms.كِتَابُ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of paternal and maternal uncles according to the Book of Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the authority of the 'Book of Ali' (Kitab Ali), a specialized legal text attributed to Imam Ali (AS) that was preserved within the scholarly circles but not widely disseminated, underscoring the depth of the Ahl al-Bayt's independent juridical reasoning. It establishes a specific inheritance distribution where the paternal uncle receives two-thirds and the maternal uncle one-third, a ruling that reflects the Shia emphasis on the nuanced application of Quranic principles through the Imams' teachings. This narration serves as a key evidence for the validity of the Imams' legal compilations alongside the Quran in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, all of them from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about something from the Obligations (legislated shares of inheritance), so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> bring out for you a Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup>?’ So I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘The Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> is not studied’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Muhammad! The Book of Ali<sup>asws</sup> is not studied?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> brought it out, and it was a splendid Book, and therein was, a man who died and left his paternal uncle and his maternal uncle. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For the paternal uncle is two-thirds and for the maternal uncle is the one-third’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad all of them from ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from abu Basir who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about certain issues of ordained shares of inheritance. He (the Imam) said, ’Do you like if I show you the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam ?’ I said, ‘But the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, is no longer studied.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘O abu Muhammad, how can you say that the book of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, is no longer studied?’ He (the Imam) brought it out and it was a magnificent book. I saw in it this case, ‘A man dies and leaves behind his paternal and maternal uncles.’ It said, ‘The paternal uncle receives two-thirds and the maternal uncle receives one- third.’”
